title: Core schema data contract consumed in place
requirement: The platform consumes the database object STERP and every object of the core schema (83 objects: 1 database, 3 functions, 34 procedures, 35 tables, 4 indexes, 6 triggers) exactly as defined in the repository, with no DDL, seeding or migration (contracts 6.1-6.2). Every platform operation calls the same procedures with the same parameter names, or executes the same parameterized statements with the same predicates, ordering and lock hints, as its legacy path (contracts 6.5). The six core triggers (tr_Company_Audit, tr_AppUser_Audit, tr_UserRole_Audit, tr_RolePermission_Audit, tr_Parameter_Audit, trg_ApprovalPurchaseOrder) fire for target writes exactly as for legacy writes and are never disabled (contracts 6.8). Objects with no static production caller (core.usp_GetFxRate, core.usp_IsBusinessDay, core.usp_ScreenParty, core.usp_UiUserPrefGet/Set) remain part of the contract unchanged (SME-1213).
acceptance_criteria: Given the isolated database built by STERP-App/build/build-db.ps1, when STERP.Api and STERP.Jobs start, then the schema drift check (contracts 6.11) reports every one of the 83 core objects present with the repository columns, types, nullability and procedure parameters;Given any platform operation, when it runs against the isolated database, then SQL Server Profiler or Extended Events show only the legacy procedure names and parameter names listed in section 8 for that operation and no DDL statement;Given a target write to core.Company through generic maintenance, when it commits, then tr_Company_Audit inserts the same core.AuditLog row shape (Source TRIGGER, attributed by COALESCE(ModifiedBy, CreatedBy, SUSER_SNAME())) as the legacy write

title: Platform menu rows and page routing
requirement: The 44 core.MenuItem rows seeded by the core seeds - the top-level File, System, Reports, Window and Help menus with their children, and the top-level Finance, Debtors, Creditors, Sales and Purchasing captions (seed 07) - are served unchanged from the shared database through platform_getMenu (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-034); module menu rows belong to their slices. A menu row with a FormClass opens the page registered for that class with FormArgument as page argument: frmSpoolViewer -> page:platform/spool-viewer (argument = file path), frmGenericMaint -> page:platform/generic-maintenance (argument = MaintCode), frmMaintLauncher -> page:platform/maintenance-launcher, frmApprovals -> page:platform/approvals, frmExceptions -> page:platform/exceptions, frmAudit -> page:platform/audit, frmJobMonitor -> page:platform/job-monitor, frmEngineDiag -> page:platform/service-diagnostics, frmReportLauncher -> page:platform/report-launcher (argument = ReportCode or module). Rows without FormClass run the shell commands of contracts 9.2 ($COMPANY and $RUNAS open page:platform/sign-on). A page opens once per class and argument and is re-activated when already open (frmMain.vb:81-90). Captions keep their access keys and shortcuts (Ctrl+O View Spool File, F8 Approvals Inbox, F9 Exception Worklist, Ctrl+R Run Report, F1 Contents, Alt+F4 Exit).
acceptance_criteria: Given SYSADM signed on to STC/RDG, when the shell loads the menu, then the File, System, Reports, Window and Help branches contain the seeded rows in SortOrder with captions and shortcuts exactly as stored in core.MenuItem;Given the System > Companies menu row (FormClass frmGenericMaint, FormArgument CORE.COMPANY), when the user selects it, then page:platform/generic-maintenance opens for CORE.COMPANY and a second selection re-activates the same page;Given the Reports > Job Monitor and System > Job Monitor rows (both frmJobMonitor, no argument), when both are selected, then one job monitor page is open;Given a menu row whose FormClass has no registered page, when it is selected, then the shell shows STERP-E-0004: Screen <class> is not installed in this release.

title: Outcome envelope, problem translation and legacy failure text
requirement: The kernel owns the single outcome model every slice uses (contracts 4.6-4.7). A kernel or slice result carries returnCode, reasonCode (8), message (200), messageCount and correlationId exactly as the STCAHDR header (CA-RETURN-CODE 00 OK, 04 WARNING, 06 HOLD, 08 ERROR, 12 SEVERE, 16 NOT FOUND; CA-FAILED = 08 THRU 16, so 06 is not a failure, SME-038). Severity names and the display text follow CobolResult (Severity 'RC'+nn for other codes; Display = message, or the severity name when blank, followed by two spaces and '(reason)' when a reason exists). A procedure THROW whose text matches STERP-(E|W|I)-<code 1-8 alphanumerics>: <text> in any SqlError of the exception (first match) becomes reasonCode '<s>-<code>', severity <s> and detail <text> (BusinessRuleException.TryTranslate). On a COBOL-derived path a driver failure keeps the legacy failure text: the kernel reproduces the text the ODBC shim returned (SQLGetDiagRec message, up to 512 bytes), which for Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 carries the vendor prefix '[Microsoft][ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server][SQL Server]' before the server message [inferred from the ODBC diagnostic-record format]; the prefix is configuration (Sterp:Kernel:LegacyDriverMessagePrefix) defaulting to that value so that the eight kernel services that classify a failure as a business refusal only when the text starts with 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-' behave as in legacy (BRF-COMMON-01, SME-011). On a .NET facade path an unclassified failure is SYS0001 with the exception text (BaseForm.Guard).
acceptance_criteria: Given a slice operation whose legacy program ends RC 04 with reason SOA0012, when it is called, then HTTP 200 returns an envelope with returnCode 4, severity WARNING and reasonCode SOA0012;Given a program ending RC 06, when it is called, then HTTP 202 returns the envelope with severity HOLD and the legacy message;Given a procedure that THROWs 50021 'STERP-E-0021: That approval is no longer pending, so it cannot be decided again.', when the procedure-backed operation runs, then HTTP 422 returns application/problem+json with reasonCode E-0021, severity E and detail equal to the text after the colon;Given a COBOL-derived kernel call whose procedure THROWs 'STERP-E-0004: ...' and the default driver prefix, when the kernel classifies the failure, then the result is RC 12 reason SQL0001 with the prefixed driver text exactly as SQLIO would have produced;Given Sterp:Kernel:LegacyDriverMessagePrefix set to empty in a characterization run, when the same failure occurs, then the kernel returns the business-refusal reason of that service (for example NUM0008 RC 08), proving the switch is the only difference

title: SQLIO unit of work and statement execution (IUnitOfWork, ISqlRunner)
requirement: The kernel reproduces SQLIO for every COBOL-derived database access. Unit of work: statements run in autocommit unless the legacy program issued BEGN; BEGN switches the logical engine connection to manual commit and COMT/ROLB end the single connection-level unit and restore autocommit; there is no nesting, so a callee's COMT or ROLB ends the caller's open work (contracts 6.4, SME-013); TSTA reports 1 (autocommit) or 0. A logical engine connection lives for one API request or one job-step execution (the target equivalent of the legacy process), and cross-slice calls share it. Statements: text up to 4,000 bytes with trailing spaces trimmed; up to 40 positional parameters bound as varchar text of at most 256 characters, trailing spaces trimmed, NULL when the legacy null flag is set, formatted exactly as the legacy program moved them (numbers through SQLIO-NUM-EDIT -(12)9.9(6) or SQLIO-INT-EDIT -(17)9 then trimmed, dates as yyyymmdd text) so that SQL Server applies the same implicit conversions; slices may bind typed values only where Agent 07 parity tests prove identical results. EXEC returns 0, 100 when the driver reports no data (for example a searched UPDATE touching no row) or -1, and the row count unless execution failed; FTCH skips row-count-only results and returns columns 1..min(requested, available) as left-justified text truncated or space-padded to the caller's widths, NULL as spaces, rendered as the ODBC character conversion would (bit as '1'/'0' [inferred], SME-031); SNGL = EXEC + FTCH + CLOS returning the code of the last step performed; MORE advances result sets; CLOS closes; an unknown function returns -1, SQLSTATE HY000 and 'SQLIO: INVALID FUNCTION <code>'. Failures carry SQLSTATE and up to 512 bytes of driver text in the FR-STERP-PLATFORM-010 form. Statement slots 1-8 are scoped to the logical connection; a PREPARE on a slot frees the statement still open there (SME-014). Connection opening reproduces the login retry (up to four attempts, wait 2,000 ms x attempt, no retry on SQLSTATE 28000, 30 s login timeout). The STERP_SQLTRACE switch is replaced by structured logging (contracts 6.9).
acceptance_criteria: Given a caller that issues BEGN, inserts two rows and issues COMT, when the unit commits, then both rows are visible together and a ROLB instead leaves neither;Given a caller unit opened with BEGN that calls a kernel service whose own code issues COMT, when the caller later issues ROLB, then the rows written before the callee's COMT remain committed (SME-013 two-level characterization);Given a parameter value of 300 characters, when it is bound, then only the first 256 characters reach SQL Server;Given a fetched varchar(60) value into a 40-byte column slot and a NULL column, when FTCH returns, then the slot holds the first 40 characters and the NULL slot holds spaces;Given SNGL for a key that does not exist, when it runs, then SQLCODE is 100 and the slot is closed;Given function code ABCD, when SQLIO is called, then SQLCODE is -1, SQLSTATE HY000 and the message is SQLIO: INVALID FUNCTION ABCD

title: Permission check service (PERMCHK -> IPermissionService)
requirement: IPermissionService.Check reproduces PERMCHK function CHECK: the header is reset (program PERMCHK, RC 00, request reference COM-002) and the answer starts as not allowed; the checked user defaults to the caller's user and the site to the caller's site when blank; the permission code is upper-cased; a missing user (PRM0001), permission (PRM0002) or company (PRM0003 'Authority is always scoped to a company') is refused RC 08 without a database call; core.usp_CheckPermission(user, permission, company, site or NULL) is executed; no row gives RC 12 PRM0005 'The authority check returned no answer'; an Allowed column whose rendered text starts with '1' gives RC 00, allowed 'Y' and '<user> holds <permission> in <company>'; otherwise RC 06 PRM0006 with the procedure's Reason text (or '<user> does not hold <permission>') - a hold, not a CA-FAILED refusal (SME-038). Any other function returns RC 08 PRM0009 after validation. A SQL failure returns the driver text as message and reason text with RC 06 PRM0007 when the text starts with 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-', otherwise RC 12 SQL0001 (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-010). The procedure's refusal reasons are, in order: user not registered, not active, no role in the company or '*', does not hold the permission (each 'STERP-E-0001: ...'); core.fn_HasPermission grants when an active user has an active role in the company or '*' (site '*' or equal or no site asked) valid today holding the permission. PRM reason codes reuse PARMGET's prefix with other meanings (BRF-PERMCHK-02).
acceptance_criteria: Given ENGINEER without BOM.RELEASE in STC, when a kernel CHECK is made, then RC 06 PRM0006 is returned with the procedure reason text starting STERP-E-0001 and allowed N;Given a blank company in the header, when CHECK runs, then RC 08 PRM0003 is returned and no SQL statement is executed;Given SYSADM holding SYS.ADMIN, when CHECK runs for SYS.ADMIN in STC, then RC 00 and the message SYSADM holds SYS.ADMIN in STC are returned;Given function code LIST, when PERMCHK-equivalent is called with valid inputs, then RC 08 PRM0009 is returned

title: Posting period check service (PERIODCK -> IPeriodService)
requirement: IPeriodService reproduces PERIODCK functions CHECK and DATES (identical behaviour): header reset (PERIODCK, RC 00, COM-009), allowed 'N', override permission FIN.PERIOD.SOFTPOST on every answer, action defaulted to POST and upper-cased (echoed only), a zero posting date defaulted to the caller's business date (no clock fallback). Validation before any lookup: company (PER0001), posting date valid (PER0002), non-zero document date valid (PER0003), non-zero tax point valid (PER0004), each RC 08. The period is the first fin.Period row of the company whose StartDate..EndDate contains the posting date, read without ORDER BY together with core.fn_HasPermission(user, 'FIN.PERIOD.SOFTPOST', company, NULL); no period gives PER0005 RC 08. Decision: OPEN -> RC 00 allowed; SOFT -> RC 00 'posted as a close adjustment' when the user holds FIN.PERIOD.SOFTPOST, else RC 06 PER0006 (hold); HARD -> PER0003 RC 08; FUTURE -> PER0004 RC 08; any other status -> PER0007 RC 08 (reason codes reused with two meanings, BRF-PERIODCK-03). Unknown function PER0009 RC 08. A SQL failure: RC 12 SQL0001 unless the text starts 'STERP-E-' (then PER0006 RC 08 status CLOSED, or PER0007 RC 06 status SOFT when the text contains 'soft closed'). fin.usp_ValidatePeriod holds a second copy of the rule (BRF-PERIODCK-01, SME-1261) and is not used here.
acceptance_criteria: Given GLCLERK posting dated 2026-05-15 in STC (period 202602 HARD), when CHECK runs, then RC 08 PER0003 is returned with allowed N (demo workflow 6 step 1);Given a posting dated 2026-10-19 in STC (period 2026/07 OPEN), when CHECK runs, then RC 00 allowed Y and fiscal year 2026 period 7 are returned;Given a SOFT period and a user without FIN.PERIOD.SOFTPOST, when CHECK runs, then RC 06 PER0006 is returned and override permission FIN.PERIOD.SOFTPOST is reported;Given a zero posting date and business date 2026-10-07, when CHECK runs, then the period covering 2026-10-07 is used

title: Document numbering service (NUMGEN -> IDocumentNumberService)
requirement: IDocumentNumberService reproduces NUMGEN: header reset (NUMGEN, RC 00, COM-005), status cleared, series upper-cased; company (NUM0001) and series (NUM0002) required, VOID also number (NUM0003) and reason (NUM0004), each RC 08. NEXT with a correlation id first looks for the lowest-sequence number already issued for company, series and correlation id and returns it with its stored status (possibly VOID), RC 04 NUM0007, without drawing; a failed replay lookup prevents any draw. Otherwise core.usp_NextDocumentNumber(company, series, user, correlation or NULL) draws the number under UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK inside its own transaction only when no transaction is open (it joins the caller's unit otherwise), so a number is drawn outside the caller's unit exactly when the legacy caller drew it before its BEGN (SME-434, SME-1037); the result is number, sequence and status ISSUED. VOID executes core.usp_VoidDocumentNumber (reason, never-issued and already-void refusals STERP-E-0005; ISSUED -> VOID with audit row). The RC 16 branches NUM0005/NUM0006 are unreachable with the current procedures (BRF-NUMGEN-01) and stay unreachable. Unsupported function NUM0009 RC 08; SQL failure NUM0008 RC 08 when the text starts 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-', otherwise SQL0001 RC 12. Replay and draw are separate statements without a shared lock (SME-060, SME-1259) - reproduced.
acceptance_criteria: Given series SDES in STC with NextNumber 7, when NEXT runs without a correlation id outside any unit, then the number is drawn, NextNumber becomes 8 and status ISSUED is returned;Given a correlation id that already drew SINV00000042, when NEXT runs again with it, then SINV00000042 is returned with RC 04 NUM0007 and no number is drawn;Given an exhausted series, when NEXT runs, then the procedure refusal STERP-E-0004 is surfaced through the FR-STERP-PLATFORM-010 classification and NextNumber is unchanged;Given VOID without a reason, when it runs, then RC 08 NUM0004 is returned and no SQL is executed

title: Idempotency service (IDEMPOT -> IIdempotencyService)
requirement: IIdempotencyService reproduces IDEMPOT: header reset (IDEMPOT, RC 00, COM-015) and outcome cleared; a blank correlation id (IDM0001), BEGIN without operation (IDM0002) or END with a status other than COMPLETED/FAILED after upper-casing (IDM0003) is refused RC 08; another function IDM0004 RC 08. BEGIN executes core.usp_IdempotentBegin(correlation, operation, company or NULL, user or NULL), which locks the key row (UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK), inserts INPROGRESS for a new key (NEW), resets a FAILED key to INPROGRESS (NEW) and answers DUPLICATE for COMPLETED and INPROGRESS otherwise. Answers: STARTED RC 00 'Instruction claimed - carry on with <operation>'; COMPLETED RC 04 IDM0006 with the original result reference; INPROGRESS RC 06 IDM0007. The FAILED (RC 08 IDM0008) and unknown-outcome (RC 12 IDM0009) branches are unreachable with the current procedure and stay so (BRF-IDEMPOT-01, G09-ADV-18); no row gives RC 12 IDM0005. The BEGIN claim commits under autocommit when the caller has not begun a unit (contracts 4.8), so an abandoned claim keeps answering INPROGRESS (SME-061). END executes core.usp_IdempotentEnd(status, result reference or NULL, message or NULL) and returns status, reference and start/end times with 'Instruction recorded as <status>'. SQL failure IDM0010 RC 08 for 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-' text, else SQL0001 RC 12. The request Idempotency-Key header is the correlation id (contracts 4.5/4.8).
acceptance_criteria: Given a new Idempotency-Key, when BEGIN runs, then STARTED RC 00 is returned and core.IdempotencyKey holds the key INPROGRESS committed even if the caller later rolls back;Given a key previously ended FAILED, when BEGIN runs, then STARTED RC 00 is returned (procedure reset) and never RC 08 IDM0008;Given a key previously ended COMPLETED with result SINV00000042, when BEGIN runs, then RC 04 IDM0006 returns SINV00000042;Given a key still INPROGRESS, when BEGIN runs, then RC 06 IDM0007 (HOLD, HTTP 202 on API paths) is returned

title: Audit writer (AUDITLOG -> IAuditWriter)
requirement: IAuditWriter reproduces AUDITLOG function WRITE: header reset (AUDITLOG, RC 00, COM-013), audit id 0, blank source -> 'COBOL', sensitive normalised to 'Y'/'N', action upper-cased; refusals RC 08 without SQL: no user AUD0001, entity type or key blank (tested against spaces only, BRF-AUDITLOG-02) AUD0002, no action AUD0003; another function AUD0009 RC 08 after validation. core.usp_WriteAudit is executed with user, company, entity type, key, action, field name, old value, new value, reason, authority reference, source, correlation id (parameters 6-12 NULL when blank) and sensitive '1'/'0'; the new AuditId is returned with 'Audited <action> of <type> <key>'. SQL failure: AUD0008 RC 08 for 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-' text, else SQL0001 RC 12. A no-row answer that reads the previous call's row area (BRF-AUDITLOG-01) is accidental carried state and is not reproduced (BC-PLATFORM-07).

title: Exception raiser (EXCPRAIS -> IExceptionRaiser)
requirement: IExceptionRaiser reproduces EXCPRAIS function RAISE: header reset (EXCPRAIS, RC 00, COM-022), outputs cleared, severity and module upper-cased, priority outside 1..9 replaced by 5; refusals RC 08: company EXC0001, severity not HOLD/WARNING/ERROR EXC0002, category EXC0003, message EXC0004, neither owner user nor role EXC0005, invalid non-zero due date EXC0006; other function EXC0009. core.usp_RaiseException is executed with company, module, severity, category, message, document type/reference, site, owner user/role, priority, due date (NULL when 0), amount and quantity (NULL when 0), user and correlation id (blank values NULL); the procedure keeps one open item per company, module, category, document type and reference (update instead of insert) and names the active role holder as owner when only a role is given. After a successful raise the return code mirrors the severity: HOLD RC 06, WARNING RC 04, ERROR RC 00 (SME-059, SME-1258) with '<SEVERITY> raised on worklist: <text>'. SQL failure EXC0008 RC 08 for 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-' text, else SQL0001 RC 12.

title: Parameter service (PARMGET -> IParameterService)
requirement: IParameterService reproduces PARMGET functions GET and GETNUM: header reset (PARMGET, RC 00, COM-025), code upper-cased, as-of date defaulted to the caller's business date and then to the host clock date; blank code PRM0001 and invalid as-of date PRM0002 RC 08 without SQL. The effective row is the core.Parameter row of the code whose CompanyCode is the caller's company (or '*' when blank) in preference to '*', latest EffectiveFrom on or before the as-of date (PARMGET's own SELECT, not core.usp_GetParameter, BRF-PARMGET-01). Found: value, data type, unit, decision reference, description (first 100 bytes), owner role, effective date yyyymmdd, scope COMPANY or ALL, '<code> = <value> (<scope>)'. Not found: caller default with scope DEFAULT RC 04 PRM0004 when use-default is 'Y', else RC 16 PRM0003. Numeric flag and NUMVAL conversion when the text holds at least one digit and only digits, '.', '-', '+', spaces or low-values (BRF-PARMGET-02: '1-2' passes; the GnuCOBOL NUMVAL result for such text is characterised by Agent 07, SME-039). GETNUM refuses a non-numeric value PRM0005 RC 08 unless RC is already above 04. Unsupported function PRM0009; SQL failure PRM0008 RC 08 / SQL0001 RC 12.

title: Business calendar service (DATECALC -> IBusinessCalendar)
requirement: IBusinessCalendar reproduces DATECALC functions VALIDATE, ADDDAYS, ADDMONTH, EOMONTH, DOW, DAYSBTWN, FORMAT, PARSE, ISBUSDAY, ADDBUS, ADJUST and CACHECLR with their reason codes and messages: header reset (DATECALC, COM-026); calendar defaulted to ENG and upper-cased, never validated (an unknown code is a weekends-only calendar, SME-1257); dates valid 1601-9999 (DAT0001); ADDDAYS/ADDMONTH range DAT0005; ADDMONTH clamps to the target month's last day; EOMONTH; DOW 1 Monday..7 Sunday with English names and weekend flag; DAYSBTWN signed (DAT0002); FORMAT DDMMYYYY/ISO/YYYYMMDD or blank (DAT0003); PARSE digits of the first 10 bytes - 8 digits by format, 6 digits always DDMMYY with fixed pivot 50 and RC 04 DAT0007 (SME-053, SME-1254), other counts DAT0004; business day = not Saturday/Sunday (core.Calendar WorksSaturday/WorksSunday ignored, SME-1256) and not a holiday of the calendar (BACS uses ENG holidays, SME-1255); ADDBUS never counts the start, fails DAT0006 after more than 3,650 steps; ADJUST NEXT/PREV/NONE within 60 days (DAT0008/DAT0009/DAT0006); other function DAT0010. Holidays come from core.CalendarDay (IsBusinessDay = 0 and HolidayName not null) when CalendarDay.CalDate exists, else core.Holiday, per calendar-year with the built-in CALBUILT 2026-2028 table (ENG 24, SCT 24, NIR 30 entries, first three characters of the calendar) when the database yields no rows or the load fails; DATECALC never returns RC 12 (BR-DATECALC-023). Carried state decision (contracts 6.9): the process-lifetime cache is replaced by a per-request read with an explicit cache (TTL 5 minutes, invalidated by target calendar maintenance); the one-time table probe and the sticky 'SQL failed, use built-in for the rest of the process' indicator are accidental carry-over and are not reproduced - a load failure falls back to the built-in table for that request only (BC-PLATFORM-06, SME-029); cache counters are reported as 0 (SME-074).

title: Payment terms calculator (TERMCALC -> IPaymentTermsCalculator)
requirement: IPaymentTermsCalculator reproduces TERMCALC functions DUEDATE, GETTERMS and DISCOUNT: header reset (TERMCALC, COM-012); defaults maximum term 60 days, calendar BACS, Bacs direction NEXT, discount basis NET (basis type and terms code upper-cased; discount basis and Bacs flag compared case-sensitively, BRF-TERMCALC-04); zero invoice date takes the supply date and invalid dates are refused TRM0003; terms resolve from core.PaymentTerms by code (company row before '*' when a CompanyCode column exists), else an explicit basis, else the statutory default; an unknown code applies the statutory default with RC 04 TRM0002; due date: INVOICE invoice+days, EOM month end+days, DAYOFNEXTMONTH day 1..31 clamped (TRM0005), STATUTORY latest of invoice, supply and received + 30 days (SME-1266), other basis TRM0004; discount date invoice + discount days; discount amount (net, or net + VAT for exactly 'GROSS') x pct / 100 rounded half away to 2 places via RNDALLOC; Bacs adjustment through DATECALC ADJUST keeping the raw date (RC 04 TRM0006 when moved); long term > maximum (from invoice to final due date) sets the flag with RC 04 TRM0007; later warnings overwrite earlier ones (BRF-TERMCALC-06); dd/mm/yyyy texts and description; GETTERMS TRM0001/TRM0002 RC 16; DATECALC failure TRM0008; other function TRM0009. title: Currency converter (FXCONV -> IFxConverter)
requirement: IFxConverter reproduces FXCONV functions GETRATE, TOGBP, TOFCY and REALISED: header reset (FXCONV, COM-010); defaults rate type SPOT, quote basis FCYPERGBP, position ASSET, places 2 when 0 (so 0 places cannot be requested, BRF-FXCONV-03); currency required FX0005 and places 0..6 FX0006 RC 08. Rates are foreign units per GBP 1; GBP has rate 1 source 'BASE CURRENCY'. GETRATE needs a valid rate date (FX0007) and reads the latest core.FxRate (UnitsPerGBP) of currency and type on or before it, RC 04 FX0008 when from an earlier date, RC 16 FX0001 when none. A supplied rate must be non-zero (FX0001) and positive (FX0002); GBPPERFCY is refused FX0003 unless allow-invert 'Y' (entered rate kept, rate inverted and truncated to 8 decimals, RC 04 FX0004). TOGBP = foreign / rate and TOFCY = sterling x rate held to 12 decimals, rounded once half away from zero to the places through RNDALLOC, residual reported (6 decimals truncated); rate looked up only when the rate is 0 and a date is given (else FX0001). REALISED requires a positive settlement rate (FX0009, not inverted, BRF-FXCONV-01) and returns booked and settled sterling each rounded and the difference (booked - settled for LIABILITY, settled - booked otherwise). Rate text '<rate 8 decimals> <ccy> per GBP 1'. Other function FX0010. Carried state decision: the sticky 'rate table unavailable' indicator after a probe or read failure (SME-064) is not reproduced - a read failure answers RC 16 FX0001 for that call only (BC-PLATFORM-06). The staleness threshold mismatch between FX.MAX.AGE.DAYS and FX.MAXAGE.DAYS (SME-1207) concerns core.usp_CheckFxStaleness and is carried unchanged.

title: Rounding and allocation service (RNDALLOC -> IRoundingAllocator)
requirement: IRoundingAllocator reproduces RNDALLOC functions ROUND, TRUNC, UNITPRC, EXTEND and ALLOC: header reset (RNDALLOC, COM-011), maximum lines 500 returned, places 0..6 (RND0001, STMONEY factor table). ROUND = ROUND-AWAY (exact halves away from zero) keeping the input as unrounded; TRUNC toward zero; UNITPRC value / value2 held to 12 decimals (truncated) then rounded half away, zero divisor RND0006; EXTEND value x value2 held to 12 decimals then rounded once. ALLOC requires 1..500 lines (RND0002), mode exactly EQUAL or WEIGHT (RND0003, not case-folded), no negative weight (RND0004), total weight > 0 (RND0005); the absolute amount is rounded half away to whole minor units, each line gets the integer part of its share held to 9 decimals, spare units go one each to the largest 9-decimal remainders with the earlier line winning ties (SME-052, SME-1262), signs are restored (zero treated as positive) and the parts are proven against the rounded source: RND0009 RC 12 with the residual otherwise (never produced in 3,000 random allocations, SME-073), else 'Allocated in full, <n> line(s) took a spare minor unit'. Other function RND0008 RC 08. All arithmetic uses System.Decimal with the legacy intermediate precisions (contracts 7.1).
acceptance_criteria: Given ROUND of 1.005 and -1.005 at 2 places, when it runs, then 1.01 and -1.01 are returned;Given ALLOC of 0.10 EQUAL over 3 lines at 2 places, when it runs, then the parts are 0.04, 0.03, 0.03 and 1 line took a spare unit;Given ALLOC mode 'equal' in lower case, when it runs, then RC 08 RND0003 is returned;Given UNITPRC with divisor 0, when it runs, then RC 08 RND0006 is returned

title: Text utilities (STRUTIL -> CobolString helpers)
requirement: The CobolString helpers reproduce STRUTIL functions UPPER, CODE, DOCREF, MONEY, QTY and SQUEEZE: header reset (STRUTIL, COM-004); max length outside 1..200 becomes 40, blank currency GBP, blank zero policy KEEP; CODE accepts after upper-casing a non-empty code of at most max length made of A-Z 0-9 - . / _ (STR0001 empty, STR0002 too long with bad position = limit, STR0003 first bad character and position, RC 08; RC 04 STR0004 when case folding changed it); DOCREF keeps only A-Z and 0-9 of the upper-cased text (merging digit groups, SME-063, SME-1267), under exactly 'STRIP' removes the leading zeros of the trailing digit run keeping one digit, RC 04 STR0006 when changed, STR0005 when nothing remains; MONEY edits two decimals by truncation with comma separators, prefixed by the single byte X'A3' (Windows-1252 pound) without a space for GBP with symbol 'Y', else '<currency> '; QTY six decimals (SU-PLACES ignored, SME-072), trailing zeros trimmed under STRIP; SQUEEZE collapses runs of spaces/low-values and trims, not upper-cased; other function STR0009 RC 08.
acceptance_criteria: Given DOCREF 'SI-000123' with STRIP, when it runs, then SI123 is returned with RC 04 STR0006;Given MONEY 1234.567 GBP with symbol Y, when it runs, then the text is X'A3' followed by 1,234.56;Given CODE 'ab c', when it runs, then RC 08 STR0003 reports the space at position 3

title: Numeric and date functions (STFUNCS -> CobolNumeric, CobolDate)
requirement: CobolNumeric and CobolDate reproduce the STFUNCS user-defined functions used in production: ROUND-AWAY(value, places) rounds to places clamped to 0..8 with exact halves away from zero (value held as S9(18)V9(12): decimals beyond 12 truncated on entry); SIGN-OF returns -1, +1 or 0; DAYS-IN-MONTH(year, month) returns the Gregorian length (28..31) and 0 outside year 1601..9999 or month 1..12; END-OF-MONTH (yyyymmdd) replaces the day with the month's last day without validating the input day (20260231 -> 20260228) and returns 0 outside the year/month domain; WEEKDAY-OF returns MOD(INTEGER-OF-DATE - 1, 7) + 1 (1 Monday..7 Sunday) and 0 for an invalid date. Arguments follow STFNARGS precision. IS-LEAP has no production route and is deferred (dispositions, SME-004). These semantics are also the contracts 7.1 ROUNDED rule (MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) used by every slice.
acceptance_criteria: Given ROUND-AWAY(2.5, 0) and ROUND-AWAY(-2.5, 0), when evaluated, then 3 and -3 are returned;Given ROUND-AWAY(1.23456, 12), when evaluated, then places are clamped to 8;Given DAYS-IN-MONTH(2028, 2) and DAYS-IN-MONTH(1600, 2), when evaluated, then 29 and 0 are returned;Given END-OF-MONTH(20260200), when evaluated, then 20260228 is returned;Given WEEKDAY-OF(20261019), when evaluated, then 1 (Monday) is returned

title: Command-line argument parser (CMDARGS -> ICommandLineParser)
requirement: ICommandLineParser reproduces CMDARGS for every batch program: functions CMDLINE (the program's command-line text, at most 256 bytes) and PARSE (supplied text) tokenise at spaces or low-values outside double quotes, remove every double quote, keep at most 80 bytes per token and ignore the first token when it has no '='; a later token without '=' is refused CMD0001 and one starting with '=' CMD0002, each RC 08 with CA-MSG-COUNT + 1 and parsing continues; each valid token yields a key of at most 12 bytes upper-cased and a value of at most 60 bytes with case preserved; the first 20 pairs are stored and more are counted as dropped (RC 04 CMD0004 '<n> argument(s) ignored - only 20 are held', which downgrades an earlier RC 08, BRF-CMDARGS-02); an unclosed quote returns RC 08 CMD0003; otherwise the message becomes '<n> argument(s) read', overwriting the CMD0001/CMD0002 text (BRF-CMDARGS-01, SME-051). Named fields: CO and COMPANY -> CO (10), SITE (10), USER (20), ASAT (8), FROM (8), TO (8), PERIOD (6), MODE (10, value upper-cased), OUT (60), last occurrence wins; GET returns the first stored occurrence (BRF-CMDARGS-03, SME-1253) or RC 16 'No argument <key> was supplied'; other function CMD0009 RC 08. In the target the command-line text is the one built by the submission path (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-057), so key drift between launchers and programs (SME-016) is reproduced as is.
acceptance_criteria: Given the command line 'TBRPT CO=STC YEAR=2026 MODE=preview', when CMDLINE runs, then CO=STC and MODE=PREVIEW are set, three pairs are stored and the message is '3 argument(s) read' (the first token is ignored);Given 'X CO=A CO=B', when parsed, then the named field CO is B and GET CO returns A;Given 'X BAD CO=STC', when parsed, then RC 08 reason CMD0001 is kept but the message reads 1 argument(s) read;Given 21 valid pairs, when parsed, then 20 are stored, RC 04 CMD0004 and '1 argument(s) ignored - only 20 are held' are returned

title: Output path resolver (RUNPATH -> IOutputPathResolver)
requirement: IOutputPathResolver reproduces RUNPATH functions BASE and BUILD: header reset (RUNPATH, COM-018), path outputs cleared, blank use-timestamp defaults to 'Y', folder upper-cased. The run directory is the configured target output root (the STERP_RUN equivalent, contracts 8.5, source ENV) or the relative 'run' (source DEFAULT) with one trailing separator removed, returned for every function with 'Run directory <base>'. BUILD maps folder to sub-directory and default extension (SPOOL spool .lst, BACS bacs .txt, MTD mtd .json, EINVOICE einvoice .xml, EXTRACTS extracts .csv, LOGS logs .log, WORK work .tmp; other RUN0001), requires a report id (RUN0002), uses the caller's extension when given, a caller stamp verbatim (untrimmed, BRF-RUNPATH-01) or the local clock yyyymmddhhmmss when stamping is exactly 'Y', and builds '<base>\<sub>\<id>-<company>-<stamp>.<ext>' (company and stamp parts omitted when blank or off) with 'Output file <path>'; other function RUN0009. Report id and company reference are concatenated without any path check (BRF-RUNPATH-02); the target reproduces the same path text and confinement of output to the configured root is proposed as BC-PLATFORM-08 (not in force). Same-second names collide and the later run overwrites the earlier file as in legacy (SME-1167).
acceptance_criteria: Given output root C:\SourceCode\STERP-App-Modern\run, report id TBRPT, company STC and stamp on at 2026-10-19 21:05:03, when BUILD SPOOL runs, then the path is <root>\spool\TBRPT-STC-20261019210503.lst;Given folder REPORTS, when BUILD runs, then RC 08 RUN0001 is returned;Given a caller stamp '20261004', when BUILD runs, then the stamp is inserted untrimmed as in legacy

title: Job run registry (JOBLOG -> IJobRunRegistry)
requirement: IJobRunRegistry reproduces JOBLOG functions START and END for every program that registered itself: header reset (JOBLOG, COM-014) with job name and status upper-cased in the caller's area; START needs a job name (JOB0001 RC 08) and executes core.usp_JobRunStart(job name, company, user as SubmittedBy, site, arguments; blank values NULL), returning the run id, status RUNNING and the start time with 'Job <name> registered as run <id>'; END needs a positive run id (JOB0002) and a status COMPLETE, WARNING, FAILED or CANCELLED (JOB0003), maps COMPLETE -> OK and CANCELLED -> ABENDED, executes core.usp_JobRunEnd(run id, status, return code, rows, log file, spool file, message; blank file names and message NULL) and maps the stored status back (OK -> COMPLETE, ABENDED -> CANCELLED, others unchanged) with 'Job <name> ended <status>'; other function JOB0009. SQL failure: first 200 bytes of the driver text with JOB0008 RC 08 for 'STERP-E-'/'STERP-W-' text, else SQL0001 RC 12. Callers that re-initialise the area before END (run id 0) are refused JOB0002 and leave the run RUNNING (SME-009) - reproduced per program by the owning slice. JL-JOB-RUN-ID is S9(9) COMP-5 while JobRunId is bigint (BRF-JOBLOG-02); the target carries int64. A no-row answer reading the previous call's row area (BRF-JOBLOG-01) is not reproduced (BC-PLATFORM-07). Registration timing for target runs follows FR-STERP-PLATFORM-057.
acceptance_criteria: Given START for job TBRPT with company STC, user GLCLERK and arguments 'CO=STC YEAR=2026', when it runs, then a core.JobRun row with Status RUNNING, SubmittedBy GLCLERK and those arguments is inserted and its id returned;Given END with status COMPLETE and return code 0, when it runs, then the row ends with Status OK and the caller sees COMPLETE;Given END with run id 0, when it runs, then RC 08 JOB0002 is returned and no row changes;Given END with status CANCELLED, when it runs, then core.JobRun Status is ABENDED

title: Batch program conventions (console messages, spool heading, suite housekeeping)
requirement: The kernel provides the batch-program conventions every re-implemented batch program uses: (a) console messages 'STERP-<I|W|E>-nnnn <text>' written to the run console (stdout/stderr equivalent) in the same order and text as the legacy DISPLAY statements, the final spool line 'STERP-I-SPOOL <full path>' for every spool the legacy program announced (programs that never announced one, for example KITRDY, KITDOCP and BOMRP010, keep not announcing it, SME-1154, SME-1735), and the return-code convention 0/4/8/12/16 with MODE PREVIEW by default (STBATLOG); (b) the 132-column Report Writer page heading of STRPTHDR - line 1 company name (40) at column 1, report id (12) at column 50, 'Page ' at 112 and the page number (ZZZ9) at 117; line 2 'Registered number: ' + number (10) and 'Place of registration: ' at 32 + place (24) at 57; line 3 title (60), 'Run date ' at 104 and dd/mm/yyyy at 113; line 4 subtitle (60), as-at text (30) at 70, user (20) at 104 and run time at 125; line 5 blank; line 6 132 dashes; detail from line 7 - with the run date and time taken from the clock as in legacy; (c) the FIN and XMD suite housekeeping (FINBATPR, XMDBATPR): standard arguments via CMDARGS with the suite's literal defaults when blank (FIN: company STC, user GLCLERK, as-at today), JOBLOG START with job name = report id and arguments = the 256-byte command line, JOBLOG END with 0 -> COMPLETE, 4 -> WARNING, other -> FAILED plus rows and spool, spool path via RUNPATH BUILD SPOOL (report id, company, timestamp) with 'STERP-E-9201 cannot build the spool path' / 'STERP-E-9202 cannot open <path>' and RC 12 on failure, company name and registered number read from core.Company (company code when not found), period resolution from fin.Period by as-at date (0/0 when none), XMD exception raising through EXCPRAIS with 'STERP-W-9701 exception refused'. The owning slices apply these per program; literal defaults stay with the owning suite (SME-023).
acceptance_criteria: Given a FIN batch report run for STC, when the spool is written, then lines 1-6 of every page match the STRPTHDR layout column for column with the company name and registered number from core.Company;Given a FIN batch program run without CO and USER, when it starts, then the JobRun row is registered for STC and GLCLERK as in legacy;Given a program that announces its spool, when it ends, then the last STERP-I-SPOOL line of the run console names the spool file recorded in core.JobRun.SpoolFile;Given an unwritable spool path, when the program opens it, then STERP-E-9202 cannot open <path> is written to the console and the program ends RC 12

title: General ledger posting gateway (fin.JournalStage + fin.usp_PostJournal -> IGlPostingGateway)
requirement: IGlPostingGateway is the shared posting contract of the 17 production programs that stage journal lines (ACCRREL, APCLOSE, APPOST, APVAT6M, ARPOSTGL, BANKREC, DESPATCH, FINDEMO, FXREVAL, GLADJUST, JNLENTRY, KITCOMPL, OPENBAL, POPOST, REBATE, SOB2B, YEAREND) and of the 10 that call fin.usp_PostJournal. It executes on the caller's logical engine connection and unit of work (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-011): StageLine inserts one fin.JournalStage row per call under the caller's correlation id with the columns and NULLIF('' ) conversions of the caller's legacy INSERT (for example POPOST.cob:181-215: CorrelationId, LineNum, CompanyCode, AccountCode, DebitAmount, CreditAmount, CurrencyCode, DimCostCentre, DimProject, Narrative, VatCode, JobRef, SubledgerType, SubledgerRef, SourceRef, CreatedBy), amounts reaching decimal(18,2) through the same legacy text conversion; Post executes fin.usp_PostJournal with the caller's header values (company, correlation id, user, description, posting date, journal type, document date, currency, source module, source ref, event code, series code, FX rate, evidence ref; SuppressResult only where the caller set it) and returns the single result row (JournalId, JournalNumber, CompanyCode, FiscalYear, PeriodNo, TotalDebitGBP, TotalCreditGBP, Status, WasDuplicate) or 'no row'. The procedure owns its transaction only when no transaction is open, otherwise it joins the caller's unit; a repeated correlation id returns the original journal with WasDuplicate = 1 (procedure idempotency through core.IdempotencyKey). Refusals (STERP-E-0009..0017, STERP-E-0004 from numbering) are returned to the caller in the FR-STERP-PLATFORM-010 failure-text form; the caller maps them to its own legacy reason codes (for example POP0005 RC 08, POP0006 RC 12 on no row). The gateway adds no retry, validation or reason code of its own. fin.JournalStage and fin.usp_PostJournal are FIN data contract objects.
acceptance_criteria: Given POPOST staging two balanced lines under correlation C1 inside RECEIPT's open unit, when Post runs, then fin.usp_PostJournal joins that unit and a later ROLB removes the journal and the staged lines together;Given the same correlation C1 posted again after commit, when Post runs, then the original JournalNumber is returned with WasDuplicate 1 and no second journal exists;Given an unbalanced stage, when Post runs, then the failure text carries STERP-E-0011 and nothing is posted;Given a posting date in hard-closed period 202602, when Post runs, then the failure text carries STERP-E-0009

title: Database health probe (PING HEALTH -> /health/ready)
requirement: The PING HEALTH database probe is reproduced as the readiness probe of STERP.Api and STERP.Jobs (contracts 10) and as the data source of the service-status indicator: one single-row query returns DB_NAME() (30), CONVERT(varchar, SYSDATETIME(), 121) (30) and LEFT(@@VERSION, 80); success is OK ('ENGINE AND DATABASE AVAILABLE'); a failure is a warning RC 04 with reason SQL0001 and the first 200 bytes of the failure text, not an error (BR-PING-002, SME-2275). PING never resets the reason code on success (BRF-PING-01) - irrelevant in the target because each call starts with a fresh outcome. The engine version literal 'STERP ENGINE 4.2.17' and the ECHO numeric round-trip belong to the COBOL engine and are replaced by the service version and excluded respectively (dispositions).
acceptance_criteria: Given the isolated database is reachable, when GET /health/ready runs, then it reports Healthy and the probe returns the database name STERP, a style-121 server time and the first 80 characters of @@VERSION;Given the database is stopped, when the probe runs, then the probe result is a warning with reason SQL0001 and the readiness check reports Unhealthy

title: Session sign-on, access list, business date and fiscal period
requirement: platform_getSession resolves the authenticated Windows login with core.usp_GetUserContext @WindowsLogin (result set 1: UserCode, DisplayName, WindowsLogin, EmailAddress, JobTitle, DefaultCompanyCode, DefaultSiteCode, IsReadOnly, IsActive, BusinessDate; result set 2: CompanyCode, CompanyName, SiteCode, SiteName, Nation, CalendarCode, BaseCurrency in company/site order) and returns the session context the legacy SterpSession held: user code, display name (user code when blank), Windows login, isSysAdm (user code = 'SYSADM'), realUserCode, title ('<user> (as <real>)' when running as another user), the access list, the selected company/site (X-STERP-Company/X-STERP-Site when supplied and present in the list, otherwise the first list entry, as SignOnAs selected Access(0)), the business date (X-STERP-Business-Date or today) and the fiscal period of the selected company for that date - first fin.Period row with the date between StartDate and EndDate ordered by FiscalYear, PeriodNo - as fiscalYear, periodNo, status and periodText 'yyyy/pp' (no period, or fin.Period missing, gives blank values; a read failure is swallowed as in legacy). A login without an active STERP user is refused 403 API0010 'No STERP user is mapped to <login>.' (the legacy degraded fallback is excluded, Q-SEC-02). platform_signOn confirms the selection: company/site must be in the access list (403 API0002, as RESTRICT is refused CAL/LIV), the period is loaded for the business date and the SIGNON note is written best effort through core.usp_WriteAudit (UserCode = session user, CompanyCode = chosen company, EntityType 'SESSION', EntityKey = user code, Action 'SIGNON', Reason 'Signed on to <CO>/<SITE>', Source 'STERP.exe'; a write failure never fails the sign-on). page:platform/sign-on reproduces frmLogin: Windows login, 'CODE   Display name', Continue as list (enabled only when the real user is SYSADM, FR-STERP-PLATFORM-032), access list, business date dd/MM/yyyy (today on first sign-on, the current date when reopened from $COMPANY/$RUNAS), messages '<n> company/site combination(s) available.', '*** No company or site has been granted to this user.' (OK disabled), '*** Select the company and site to work in.'; OK or double-click confirms, Cancel leaves the session unchanged; when reopened the current company/site stays selected. The status-bar fields User, Co, Site, 'Period: yyyy/pp STATUS' (or '-') and business date come from this context (contracts 9.1).
acceptance_criteria: Given Windows login mapped to RESTRICT, when GET /api/platform/v1/session runs, then the access list contains only STC/RDG and the selected company is STC/RDG;Given RESTRICT, when sign-on is posted for CAL/LIV, then 403 API0002 is returned and no SIGNON audit row is written (demo workflow 5 step 4);Given SYSADM signing on to STC/RDG with business date 2026-10-19, when sign-on succeeds, then the context shows fiscal period 2026/07 OPEN and one core.AuditLog row EntityType SESSION Action SIGNON Reason 'Signed on to STC/RDG' Source STERP.exe exists;Given an unmapped Windows login, when the session is requested, then 403 API0010 'No STERP user is mapped to DOMAIN\user.' is returned;Given core.usp_WriteAudit fails, when sign-on is posted, then sign-on still succeeds

title: Continue as another user (SYSADM run-as)
requirement: platform_continueAsUser reproduces LoginService.RunAs: only a session whose real user is SYSADM may continue as another user - otherwise 403 API0003 with the legacy text 'Only SYSADM may continue as another user.'; the target user's context is loaded with core.usp_GetUserContext @UserCode (an unknown or inactive code is refused 403 API0010 'No STERP user is mapped to <code>.' instead of the legacy stand-alone fallback, Q-SEC-02); on success the real user stays SYSADM, isSysAdm becomes true only when the chosen code is SYSADM itself, the permission cache is cleared, the access list is replaced and its first entry selected, and the RUNAS note is written best effort through core.usp_WriteAudit (UserCode = the chosen user, CompanyCode = the chosen user's first company, EntityType 'SESSION', EntityKey = chosen code, Action 'RUNAS', Reason 'SYSADM continued the session as <code>', Source 'STERP.exe'). platform_listRunAsUsers returns the active users ordered by UserCode (UserCode, DisplayName) for the Continue as list and is refused 403 API0003 unless the real user is SYSADM (the list is only offered to SYSADM). After run-as the GUI sends X-STERP-Run-As on every request (contracts 4.5, 5.2); choosing the user already in effect does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Given SYSADM continuing as PURMGR, when run-as is posted, then the context user is PURMGR, the title is 'PURMGR (as SYSADM)', the access list is PURMGR's and one SESSION/RUNAS audit row attributed to PURMGR exists;Given BUYER, when run-as is posted, then 403 API0003 with 'Only SYSADM may continue as another user.' is returned;Given SYSADM requesting run-as for an inactive user code, when it is posted, then 403 API0010 is returned and the session is unchanged;Given SYSADM, when the run-as user list is requested, then all active users are returned ordered by UserCode

title: Permission probe for GUI enabling
requirement: platform_checkPermissions answers, for each permission code supplied, whether the session user (or run-as user) holds it in the session company and site, exactly as LoginService.HasPermission: a blank code is allowed without a database call; otherwise core.usp_CheckPermission(@UserCode, @PermissionCode, @CompanyCode, @SiteCode) is executed and allowed = the Allowed bit of the returned row (no row = not allowed), with the procedure's Reason text. The GUI keeps a per-session cache that is cleared whenever the user, company or site changes (SignOnAs and SelectCompanySite cleared it) and uses the answers only to enable or hide actions; every business operation still performs its own legacy checks (contracts 5.4). Legacy fails open: an exception during the check left the action enabled and cached as allowed; the API returns 500 SYS0001 for a database failure and the GUI treats a failed probe as allowed (parity) until BC-PLATFORM-01 is approved.
acceptance_criteria: Given SALESREP in CAL/LIV, when AR.CREDIT.OVERRIDE and SO.ORDER.ENTER are probed, then AR.CREDIT.OVERRIDE is not allowed and SO.ORDER.ENTER is allowed (demo workflow 5 step 2);Given CREDMGR, when AR.CREDIT.OVERRIDE is probed, then it is allowed;Given a blank code in the list, when probed, then it is reported allowed and no procedure call is made for it

title: Menu bar load
requirement: platform_getMenu executes core.usp_UiMenuLoad @UserCode, @CompanyCode, @SiteCode for the session (or run-as) user, company and site and returns its rows unchanged and in its order (ISNULL(ParentMenuCode, ''), SortOrder, Caption): active rows whose PermissionCode is empty or granted through core.usp_UiCheckAccess (fn_HasPermission, falling back to usp_CheckPermission, a security check that cannot be answered denies), with every branch the filter emptied removed repeatedly and orphans removed; columns MenuCode, ParentMenuCode, Caption, FormClass, FormArgument, PermissionCode, SortOrder, Shortcut. As in MenuService.Load a failure returns an empty list (the shell then shows its built-in menu).
acceptance_criteria: Given a user without SYS.ADMIN, when the menu is loaded, then System > Engine Diagnostics is absent and every other System row the user holds is present;Given a branch whose children are all filtered out, when the menu is loaded, then the branch row is absent;Given the database is unavailable, when the menu is requested, then 200 with an empty list is returned

title: Field lookups (F2) through named lookup sources
requirement: Lookups are fixed, named queries; no SQL text or procedure name is ever accepted from the client (contracts 6.2). platform_lookupMasterFile reproduces the generic F2 lookup of every registered master file: core.usp_UiLookup(@CompanyCode, @SiteCode, @Search, @Argument = MaintCode) -> core.usp_UiMaintList with @ForLookup = 1 and @Top = 200: blank argument STERP-E-0099, unregistered STERP-E-0090, table not installed STERP-E-0092 (422); no maintain permission is required; columns are the IsInList or IsKey columns present on the table in SortOrder, ColumnName order; company-scoped definitions return rows of the session company or '*'; a search matches LIKE '%search%' on searchable or key TEXT/CODE columns (empty search = all; SqlHelper sends '' as NULL); rows are ordered by the key columns. It serves the MaintColumn.LookupProc/LookupArg lookups (CORE.CALENDAR, CORE.COMPANY, CORE.CURRENCY, CORE.MAINTDEF, CORE.ROLE, CORE.SITE, CORE.USER, ITM.ITEM, ITM.UOM, ITM.WAREHOUSE) and the form lookups ITM.ITEM, FIN.ACCOUNT and FIN.BANK. platform_lookupNamed serves the four non-maintenance lookups of the forms - AR.CUSTOMER (DebtorsService.CustomerPickSql), SO.ORDER (SalesOrderService.OrderPickSql), SO.PICKLIST (SalesOrderService.PickListPickSql) and PO.OPENORDERS (po.usp_OpenOrders with @Argument = company) - each implemented by its owning slice through the ILookupSource contract with the same predicates, ordering and parameters (@CompanyCode, @SiteCode, @Search, @Argument); while the owning slice is not delivered the lookup returns 501 API0501. Results keep the result-set column order; the first column is the code returned to the field. page:platform/lookup reproduces frmLookup: title 'Lookup - <caption>', Find box and Search button (Enter searches), grid, '<n> record(s).  Double-click or press Enter to select.', OK or double-click returns the first column trimmed, Cancel returns nothing; an error shows '*** <message>' in the count line instead of a dialog.
acceptance_criteria: Given STC and ITM.ITEM with search BIKE, when the master-file lookup runs, then at most 200 item rows whose searchable text contains BIKE are returned in key order and the first column is the item code;Given lookup code NOSUCH, when the master-file lookup runs, then 422 with reason E-0090 is returned;Given a user without ITM.ITEM.MAINT, when the ITM.ITEM lookup runs, then rows are returned (lookups need no maintain permission);Given AR not yet delivered, when the named lookup AR.CUSTOMER is requested, then 501 API0501 names slice STERP-AR;Given the lookup page, when the operator presses Cancel, then the field keeps its value

title: Approvals inbox
requirement: platform_listApprovals executes core.usp_UiApprovalInbox(@CompanyCode = session company, @UserCode = session user, @Status) and returns its rows in its order (RequestedAt descending): ApprovalId, CompanyCode, DocumentType, DocumentRef, ApprovalType, Amount, RequestedBy, RequestedAt, Status, AgeDays (days since the request on the server clock). The status filter offers PENDING (default), APPROVED, REJECTED, INVALIDATED and ALL; ALL or blank returns every status. The procedure ignores @UserCode, so every approval of the company is listed whoever asks (observed), and no permission is checked on this path (the menu row needs SYS.APPROVAL.VIEW but the toolbar button opens the inbox without a check, frmMain.vb:184-205). page:platform/approvals reproduces frmApprovals as a list page (filters row Status; toolbar Refresh (F5), Approve (F10), Reject, Close (F3); '<n> record(s)'); changing the status reloads.
acceptance_criteria: Given PURMGR signed on to STC/BHM, when the inbox is listed with PENDING, then the pending request for PO00000002 is listed (demo workflow 3 step 3);Given status ALL, when listed, then approvals of every status of the session company are returned in RequestedAt descending order;Given a user who is not an approver, when the inbox is listed, then the same rows are returned (no user filter, observed)

title: Approval decision

title: Restart a job stream from a step
requirement: jobs_restartRun reproduces the operator's legacy restart - resubmitting the same stream with RESTART=<label> - for a stream run the target executed: it re-submits the stream with the original command line from the run manifest plus ' RESTART=<label>' through the same entry point and checks (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-057), so the new run registers a new core.JobRun row, MAXCC starts at 0 and execution jumps to the label and continues to the end with the normal COND gating (if %LASTCC% GEQ 8 goto ABEND). Labels are the stream's STEPnnn labels and ABEND and EOJ (RESTART=EOJ ends at once with MAXCC 0, RESTART=ABEND writes 'STREAM TERMINATED BY COND CODE 0' and ends). A run the target did not execute, or that is not a stream, cannot be restarted through this resource (422 API0023 - the legacy Arguments column keeps only MODE, ASAT, YEAR and PERIOD, so the parameters cannot be rebuilt); a label unknown to the stream definition is refused 422 API0024 by this resource only. The response is 202 JobRunAccepted for the new run.

title: Job stream engine (SETENV, RUNSTEP, JOBEND)
requirement:
The stream engine reproduces the three platform procedures every stream uses; stream scripts (step lists, inline lookups, conditional parameters, custom jumps) are owned by the business slices and call these primitives. Prologue (SETENV): parameters are parsed from the command line as cmd.exe passes them - a quoted 'KEY=VALUE' token or an unquoted KEY followed by VALUE as the next token - into P_ variables (later wins), with defaults CO=STC, USER=OPS, MODE=PREVIEW, DAYS=0 and SITE, ASAT, PERIOD, YEAR, RUN, STAGE, VATPER, RESTART, SUN, STYLE empty; the stamp yyyyMMddHHmmss is taken from the clock; ASAT defaults to the stamp date; PERIOD and YEAR default from the clock month with an April fiscal start (month >= 4: period = month - 3, else period = month + 9 and year - 1); PP is the two-digit period, YYYYPP = YEAR + PP; PEREND = EndDate yyyymmdd of fin.Period(CO, YEAR, PERIOD), else ASAT; the run folders logs, spool, bacs, mtd, einvoice, extracts and work exist; SYSOUT = \logs\-.log starts with the job card lines (// JOB (STERP),' SERVICE',CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=X; SUBMITTED, COMPANY/SITE/MODE/ASAT, FISCAL YEAR/PERIOD/RUN, STERP_HOME, SYSOUT, //JOBLIB, blank line); the console line 'STERP-I-0001 started - SYSOUT '; LASTCC = MAXCC = 0; the stream registers with core.usp_JobRunStart(@JobName = stream, @CompanyCode = CO, @SubmittedBy = USER, @Arguments = 'MODE= ASAT= YEAR= PERIOD=

') and SYSOUT records '//* core.JobRun id '. Step (RUNSTEP): SYSOUT gets '// EXEC PGM=,PARM=''' and '//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*', the console 'STERP-I-0002 '; an @SQL step executes its fixed, parameterised statement (SET NOCOUNT ON) with its result sets and messages appended to SYSOUT and any failure giving COND 8; a program step runs the delivered batch program with PARM as its command line, its console output appended to SYSOUT, COND = its return code; MAXCC = max; SYSOUT '//* ENDED - COND CODE (MAXCC )' and, for COND >= 8, the console 'STERP-E-0008 failed - COND CODE '. Gating after every step: COND >= 8 goes to ABEND, 0 and 4 continue. ABEND writes '//* STREAM TERMINATED BY COND CODE ' then JOBEND; EOJ runs JOBEND. Epilogue (JOBEND): status OK, WARNING (MAXCC >= 4), FAILED (>= 8), ABENDED (>= 12); SYSOUT end lines ('//* JOB ENDED - MAXIMUM COND CODE ()', date/time, '//'); console 'STERP-I-0009 ended - MAXCC () - '; core.usp_JobRunEnd(@Status, @ReturnCode = MAXCC, @LogFile = SYSOUT, @Message 'Job stream ended with COND code ') when registered, errors ignored; the stream's return code is MAXCC. RESTART=

title: Operator console: access, menu, paging and messages
requirement: page:platform/operator-console replaces the STERPOPS screen-section console started by jobs\OPSCON.cmd. Sign-on: the console identity is the authenticated Windows user resolved as in FR-STERP-PLATFORM-031 (the legacy typed user code without credential, three-attempt lock and unvalidated typed company are replaced by contracts 5.1-5.3; SME-1170, SME-1171), with company and site from the session and the read-only flag = core.AppUser.IsReadOnly (first character '1'). Main menu options in legacy order: 1/A submit a job, 2/B job monitor, 3/C exception queue, 4/D period status, 5/E engine health, X/END/F3/ESC sign off (other input 'STERP-W-2001'). Lists hold at most 300 rows, are shown 15 per page (F7/PgUp/'-'/'P' back, F8/PgDn/'+'/'N' forward, never past the last page start, floor 1; typed number = absolute row, fractions truncated, outside 1..n 'STERP-W-9001'/'STERP-W-9002'), and keep the legacy message texts STERP-<I|W|E>-nnnn (BR-STERPOPS-041). The console's session-start date (used for ASAT pre-fill and the health business date) is the date the page was opened, sent explicitly by the page (SME-1178). Function keys are always available (COB_SCREEN_EXCEPTIONS no longer matters), so the legacy refresh that undid paging in the job monitor and period lists (SME-1179) does not arise; the explicit Refresh action reloads and returns to row 1. The page has no core.MenuItem row (none is seeded; data frozen) and is reached by its route /operator-console and from the job monitor page.

title: Operator console: job catalogue and submission
requirement: platform_listConsoleCatalogue reproduces the console catalogue: SELECT ReportCode, Module, ProgramName, ISNULL(ParamSpec,''), LEFT(Title,40) FROM core.ReportDef WHERE IsActive = 1 ORDER BY CASE WHEN ReportCode LIKE 'JOB.%' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, Module, ReportCode, at most 300 rows, PermissionCode neither selected nor checked (SME-1173), message 'STERP-I-3000 <n> RUNNABLE DEFINITIONS IN THE CATALOGUE'. The parameter panel splits ParamSpec at commas into at most eight entries, cuts each to 14 characters, trims, upper-cases and splits at '=' into key and fixed default (24); pre-fill: CO = session company and USER = session user always, SITE = session site and ASAT = session-start date (yyyymmdd) and MODE = PREVIEW only when the spec gives no default (an explicit 'MODE=' becomes PREVIEW), others the default or blank; every value including CO and USER is editable (SME-1174); F3/ESC or 'X' as the first value cancels ('STERP-I-3201 SUBMISSION CANCELLED'). platform_submitConsoleJob (STERP.Jobs) builds the legacy console command line: ' KEY=VALUE' for every non-blank key and value, unquoted, so a value containing a space becomes two arguments (SME-1175), truncated to 200 characters; ReportCode beginning exactly 'JOB.' (case-sensitive) runs the stream ProgramName, otherwise the program ProgramName; the read-only flag does not restrict submission (SME-1172). The console registers nothing itself: the job's own registration is the run (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-057). Completion panel: the console waited synchronously; the page polls the run (jobs_getRun) until its execution state is ENDED or LOST, then makes the completion read (platform_getConsoleLastRun, STERPOPS 3400-LAST-RUN): SELECT TOP 1 Status, ISNULL(SpoolFile,ISNULL(LogFile,'')) FROM core.JobRun WHERE JobName = ProgramName ORDER BY JobRunId DESC - the newest row of that name for any user, company or time (SME-1177) - status cut to 12 and path to 108 characters, no row or a failed read -> UNKNOWN and ''; it shows 'STERP-I-3301 <ReportCode> ENDED RC=<rc> STATUS=<status> SPOOL=<path>' with RC = the process exit code in three digit positions and a floating minus (1000 -> 0, 9009 -> 9, 12345 -> 345, SME-1176); job outcomes never change any console exit code. EXE launches wrote their console output to run\logs\OPS-<PROG>-<session stamp>.log (overwritten by a second launch, SME-1187); the target writes the run console to <root>\logs\OPS-<PROG>-<session stamp>.log with the same overwrite rule and records it as LogFile only through the program's own registration as legacy did.
acceptance_criteria: Given OPS for STC, when MONTHEND is submitted with YEAR=2026 PERIOD=7 MODE=PREVIEW, then 202 is returned, the stream registers its own core.JobRun row with SubmittedBy OPS and the completion panel later shows status WARNING and the SYSOUT path (demo workflow 6 step 6);Given ParamSpec 'CO,USER,MODE,ASAT' for JOB.NIGHTLY, when the panel is built, then CO and USER are the session values, MODE is PREVIEW and ASAT is the page-open date;Given ParamSpec entry 'RESTART=STEP010', when the panel is built, then key RESTART gets default STEP01 (14-character cut);Given a value 'A B' for key STAGE, when submitted, then the command line contains STAGE=A B unquoted;Given a read-only user, when a job is submitted, then the submission is accepted;Given no core.JobRun row named KITRDY, when the completion read is made for program KITRDY, then status UNKNOWN and an empty path are returned

title: Operator console: exception queue and acknowledgement
requirement: platform_listConsoleExceptions reproduces the console exception queue: SELECT ExceptionId, CompanyCode, Module, Severity, LEFT(Category,24), LEFT(Message,60), Status, ISNULL(AgeDays) FROM core.ExceptionItem WHERE Status <> 'RESOLVED' ORDER BY Priority, ExceptionId, all companies, at most 300 rows, stored AgeDays fetched but not shown, message 'STERP-I-5000 <n> OPEN EXCEPTIONS' (acknowledged rows included). platform_acknowledgeConsoleException acknowledges one listed exception immediately, without confirmation: a read-only user is refused 'STERP-E-5002 READ ONLY USER MAY NOT ACKNOWLEDGE' (403 with that reason, the only use of the read-only flag); otherwise core.usp_ResolveException(@ExceptionId, @UserCode = console user, @ResolutionNote 'ACKNOWLEDGED AT THE OPERATOR CONSOLE', @Status 'ACKNOWLEDGED') sets Status ACKNOWLEDGED with no current-status precondition, overwrites the note, keeps ResolvedBy/ResolvedAt and inserts an audit row (separate autocommit statements); the response carries 'STERP-I-5001 EXCEPTION <id> ACKNOWLEDGED BY <user>' and the page reloads to the first page. An acknowledged row stays listed and can be acknowledged again (another audit row). A failure shows 'STERP-E-9009 SQL <SQLSTATE> <first 50 characters of the message>'.

requirement: The console's engine health (option 5) shows the service diagnostics of FR-STERP-PLATFORM-056 - service version instead of the COBOL engine version, database name, server time, database version - and is healthy exactly when the PING-equivalent probe is OK ('STERP-I-7000 ENGINE AND DATABASE HEALTHY'), otherwise 'STERP-E-7001 <first 60 characters of the message>' (a database warning counts as unhealthy, SME-2275); the legacy echo of 1234.56 x 2 is not reproduced (COMMAREA mapping test, SME-1190). platform_runConsoleSelfTest replaces 'OPSCON SMOKE' (and STERPOPS SMOKE/-SMOKE): it signs on the requested user (default OPS) with the requested company, and when that user is unknown or inactive reports 'STERP-W-8001 <reason>' and falls back to the first active user by UserCode (SME-1182); it returns the first 12 catalogue rows, 10 monitor rows, 10 exception rows and 12 period rows with their counts ('ROWS AVAILABLE: <n>' or '(no rows)'), the health lines and returnCode 0, or 8 when no user could be signed on, a list query failed (STERP-E-9009) or the health probe was not OK; it never submits or acknowledges. The legacy database-down RC 12 is always overwritten by 8 (SME-1181) and stays 8.

title: Service diagnostics and service status (replaces engine diagnostics)
requirement: page:platform/service-diagnostics replaces frmEngineDiag (contracts 10): platform_getServiceDiagnostics returns the service name and version, the PING-equivalent probe (database name, server time style 121, first 80 characters of @@VERSION, return code and message as in FR-STERP-PLATFORM-030), the readiness result, the schema drift-check result (contracts 6.11) and the delivered slices with their waves; the page shows them in an 'Engine and database' group with Ping (F5) and Close (F3), the status line 'Engine <severity>' with cue OK or '!'. platform_getServiceStatus returns the status-bar value with EngineService.Status semantics: ONLINE when the probe is OK and a database name was returned, DEGRADED when the probe succeeded with a warning (RC <= 4), DOWN otherwise or on any exception; the shell polls it as frmMain did (contracts 9.1). The COMMAREA test (F10), the program directory list and the copybook map have no target equivalent (dispositions). Access is gated like legacy only by the menu (SYS.ADMIN) - the toolbar button opened the form without a check.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reachable database, when diagnostics are requested, then the database name STERP, a server time and the version text are returned with status ONLINE;Given the database is stopped, when the status is requested, then DEGRADED or DOWN is returned according to whether the probe answered with a warning or failed;Given a drift between the repository contract and the database, when diagnostics are requested, then the differences are listed

title: Job submission framework and run lifecycle for all slices
requirement: Every job submission - a slice's POST /api/<segment>/v1/jobs/<JOBCODE>/runs, the catalogue launch (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-044), the console submission (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-051) and a restart (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-048) - goes through IJobSubmission in STERP.Jobs and follows one lifecycle (contracts 8.3): (1) authenticate and resolve the STERP user and context headers; (2) refuse with 501 API0501 when the program or any stream step belongs to an undelivered slice; (3) run the checks the legacy program performed before its own registration (declared per job by the owning slice), returning 422 with the legacy return/reason code and message and registering nothing when they refuse; (4) build the command line by the entry point's legacy rule (slice job: typed parameters in schema order through the ReportService.BuildArguments rule with USER defaulting to the caller; catalogue: FR-STERP-PLATFORM-044; console: FR-STERP-PLATFORM-051; stream step: the PARM text) - the program parses it with ICommandLineParser (FR-STERP-PLATFORM-025); (5) register exactly as the legacy entry point did: the program's own JOBLOG START values (job name, company, user, site, arguments) for a self-registering program, the SETENV values for a stream, the launcher row first for a catalogue launch, and one row named after the job code for a program that never registered itself (contracts 8.3); (6) write the run manifest and return 202 JobRunAccepted with Location /api/jobs/v1/runs/{jobRunId}; (7) execute immediately on its own worker with no queue limit, no time-out and no automatic retry (legacy launches were independent processes waiting without time-out, SME-1242); (8) end the registration(s) with the legacy END values of each registering entry point. Program return codes keep 0/4/>=8. A job-host restart while a run executes marks the manifest LOST and leaves core.JobRun RUNNING, as a killed legacy process did. The target schedules nothing and never starts work by itself (contracts 6.10, 8.6).
acceptance_criteria: Given a slice job submitted with a typed parameter object, when accepted, then the command line is KEY=VALUE pairs in schema order with USER set to the caller and 202 returns the JobRunId of the program's own registration;Given a program that refuses a missing mandatory argument before it registers, when submitted without it, then 422 with the legacy reason is returned and no core.JobRun row exists;Given STERP.Jobs stopped during a run, when it restarts, then the run manifest state is LOST and core.JobRun still shows RUNNING;Given two submissions of the same job at once, when both are accepted, then both run concurrently with separate JobRunIds

title: Stock movement posting service (STKMOVE, IC-ITM-STKMOVE)
requirement: Public in-process service reproducing STKMOVE for RECEIPT, ISSUE, RETURN, ADJUST, COMPLETE, OPENING, SCRAP, TRANSFER, CONFIRM, HOLD and RELEASE with the binding algorithm of STERP-ITM.md 4.1 (reset, defaults, ordered validation, ITEMVAL CLASSCHK STOCK gate, UOMCONV TOSTOCK, LOTSER checks and registration, one inv.usp_PostStockMovement call per leg, transit, quality holds, error classification, reply); own transaction when the caller connection is in autocommit, savepoint only inside a caller transaction; procedure applocks and lock hints; return codes 00, 06, 08, 12, 16.

title: Unit conversion service (UOMCONV TOSTOCK and FACTOR, IC-ITM-UOMCONV)
